result.argument: Refutation attempted and failed. Six masking vectors were probed with executed commands, all ruled out. (1) ImportError branch: validate_canon.py:22-30 would skip schema validation and still return 0 if jsonschema were absent; but jsonschema 4.10.3 is installed and the real run prints the success line 'schema validation: OK (jsonschema)', not the skip line. (2) Schema-load failure is not silently absorbed: pointing SCHEMA at a nonexistent dir yields errors: 1 / 'schema validation failed: [Errno 2] No such file or directory' and rc=1. (3) Non-vacuity / dead schema path: I copied the live data/canon.json to a mktemp dir, injected 'bogus_injected' into ['1115']['works']['001'], redirected common.CANON_JSON and ran the real validate_canon.main() -> rc=1, 'Additional properties are not allowed (bogus_injected was unexpected)', and the dumped failing subschema shows additionalProperties:False at the works patternProperties block WITH the new source property, proving enforcement is live at the root-reachable path. (4) Control isolating the fix: removing only the new 'source' property from a schema copy and running the real main() against the real canon reproduces the exact original error 'Additional properties are not allowed (source was unexpected)' at ['1115']['works']['001'], rc=1 — so the 0-error result is produced by the fix, not by skipping validation. (5) Stale/unread data: common.read_json opens the file fresh (no cache); redirected runs consumed redirected paths, and the live canon genuinely contains the key (1115/001 keys include source; work-level source census = exactly 1, value 'local:curated'); validator reports authors: 3274 | works: 8816, so full real data was read. (6) No alternate schema: grep -rn 'canon.schema.json' shows the only loader is validate_canon.py:24 via SCHEMA = REPO/'schema'; no env override or second schema file. The central claim survives this lens.
result.counterevidence: The only input shape that would make 0 errors an artifact is the ImportError path (jsonschema absent) — and that path is selected at runtime and would print a different string. It is excludable here because the run prints 'schema validation: OK (jsonschema)' and jsonschema 4.10.3 is importable. Two structural fragilities remain, though neither makes the current 0 an artifact: (a) validate_canon.py uses short-circuiting jsonschema.validate(), so it reports only the FIRST error — a future multi-error document would understate the count as 1 (not 0), which is a reporting granularity limit, not a masking of '0'; (b) the integrity loop's only per-item guard is AID_RE/WID_RE/URN_RE plus cts_confirmed-is-bool, so a field like a null title is governed solely by the schema, which now passes. Both are latent robustness notes; neither is evidence that the observed 0 errors was fabricated by skipped validation, an unloaded schema, or unread data.

Bare type:string+minLength:1 constrains only "non-empty string"; it admits any typo/case/spacing variant of either recognised tier.

Executed counterexample (no repo file touched; fixtures in-memory + mktemp): a work {"cts_confirmed": true, "edition": "TLG lifted text", "source": "restriced:tlg"} (transposed letters) VALIDATES CLEANLY against the fixed schema (iter_errors -> 0). Feed that same work to the real consumers:
  - check_no_restricted.restricted_keys -> uris=set(), editions=set()  => firewall is BLIND ("Restricted works to guard: 0", exit 0 / OK)
  - build_jsonld._work_publishable -> True (not startswith 'restricted:' and cts_confirmed truthy)
  - build_jsonld.nt_lines -> 1 published editions line containing the restricted text "TLG lifted text" (leaks into the CC BY-SA published graph)
The correctly-spelled twin "restricted:tlg" is caught (uris={'…/1115.001'}, editions={'TLG lifted text'}, 0 leaked lines) — so the ONLY thing standing between restricted content and the published artifact here is the tier's spelling, which the schema now declines to check. Same result for "Restricted:tlg" (case).

Direct falsification of "still rejects all invalid input it rejected before": on the pre-fix schema (work-level 'source' property deleted in-memory) the input source='restriced:tlg' is REJECTED ("Additional properties are not allowed ('source' was unexpected)"); on the fixed schema it is ACCEPTED. So the fix admits a value class it previously rejected, and that class silently disables the firewall. "local:curated " (trailing space), "local", "Local:Curated" likewise all ACCEPT, all non-publishable, all invisible to the firewall.

Cheap fix was available and omitted: adding "enum": ["local:curated"] or "pattern": "^(local:curated|restricted:[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+)$" (one line) — verified to REJECT 'restriced:tlg' while still ACCEPTing both legitimate tiers and leaving every consumer and the current data (which contains only 'local:curated') untouched. The array alternative is correctly excluded (an array would break isinstance/hashability in both consumers), so the correct strict choice is a scalar with an enum/pattern — the fix chose scalar without the enum/pattern. "Complete" therefore fails: the schema does not encode the vocabulary its consumers require, and for a firewall keyed on a literal prefix that is a correctness gap, not cosmetics.

The pre-collected evidence already concedes this under "[FAIL] The schema constrains the work-level 'source' tier to the vocabulary its consumers recognise" and then discounts it as "a latent, not an active, drift." That discount is what I refute: the mode of failure is silent bypass of a restricted-content firewall and silent non-publishing of curated works, and it is reachable the moment a supplement contains one mistyped tier — a much narrower failure surface than "no further latent drift remains" asserts.
